You're starting with a lot more capital than I did. I went with the basic minimum metals people recommended (1 ozt gold, 100 ozt silver) and then used the rest on stocks/crypto. It happened to be that I chose well and the crypto I picked outpaced stocks and metals by a considerable amount. Doesn't mean it'll be the same for you.
Spend the hours reading the whitepapers and roadmaps. Think about how you might rotate gains from one asset into another and consider why one will take off before the other. You won't see every opportunity unless you're spending 16-24 hours a day looking for stuff as it launches, but new opportunities keep coming too.
The important thing is to understand stuff before you buy. You're not going into debt so the gains will outweigh the losses. You repeat this process as long as you want at the pace you choose. People spend a lot of time looking into a PC build, a new vehicle, expensive appliance and so on. Do that for investments. Investing is just one big learning process.
